_note: HASHES ARE CORPUS-SPECIFIC. This oracle describes the envelope published over the GENERATED bench corpus named below, and nothing else. It does NOT replace, reconcile or re-take either historical per-store envelope reference — the #566 one recorded in docs/dashboard-gotchas.md and the #582 one in docs/backend-performance.md section 7. Those were captured against the maintainer's private store and their values are deliberately not restated here, because this file is published to the public mirror and one of those documents is private. Comparing a value here against a value there is meaningless.

build_provenance._note: WHICH TREE built the corpus these numbers were measured over (#718). The producer digest is a sha256 over framed (path, file sha256) records for the closed manifest in bin/build-bench-fixtures.py (PRODUCER_SOURCES). Before it existed, `_marker_payload` recorded only the PARAMETERS of a build, so two trees agreeing on seed, scale, pricing date, stats epoch and params_hash shared one corpus root and the second published an envelope the first tree's ingest produced. The corpus fingerprint could not see it, because `semantic_hash` is computed over semantic columns and both ingests agree on every one of them. RECORDED, NOT GATED: `--verify` reports this digest beside the current tree's and does not fail on a difference. The recorded numbers describe the published envelope, which is stable across most producer changes, so gating here would fail bin/cctally-envelope-oracle-test on roughly every commit that touches bin/ and make re-stamping this field a per-commit chore. What IS gated is the corpus actually measured: `--verify` refuses when its provenance is absent, malformed, or names a producer other than the tree under test. SHAPE, and why the version key is named differently from the marker's: this object is a SUMMARY of the marker's `build_provenance` and carries `source_count` where the marker carries the `sources` list, so it must never be fed to `_provenance_failure`, which would report it as a producer digest over no sources. Sharing the marker's `schema_version: 1` over a different shape is what made that confusion available. The per-source list is deliberately not restated here — it lives in the corpus marker at data/.bench-fixture.json, and 12 KB of path/digest pairs in a mirrored file would churn on every bin/ commit while adding nothing this field is read for.

envelope._raw_sha256_note: A raw sha256 over the whole envelope is deliberately NOT recorded. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (#750 S1): the earlier note said it 'differs between machines', and the four-run measurement described under reproducibility.verified_on disproves that as a categorical claim — both LAN runners produced the same raw digest within each tested tree. What remains true is that it does not survive a corpus rebuild, because rebuild- and process-derived fields (`data_version`, `sync_activity.server_epoch`) are deliberately present in it, and that `doctor` makes it host-derived in principle even where two hosts happened to agree. That is why the stable digest is the oracle. bin/cctally-snapshot-measure still prints the raw value, which is the right tool for a before/after comparison across a code change with one built corpus left in place.
envelope._codex_leg_is_asserted: Every capture runs assert_snapshot_renders_the_codex_cycle over the measured snapshot, so a recorded envelope can never be the degraded short branch: availability ok, no codex_cycle_unavailable, a hero cycle with non-zero spend.

envelope._622_portability_retake: #622 moved BOTH envelope values while the corpus fingerprint remained fixed by making the corpus identity and ingest order platform-independent. Before the fix, macOS used the logical /tmp spelling while the generator had persisted /private/tmp: the Codex containment check therefore withheld session metadata, and physical-path hashes changed every opaque provider/file identity. Linux also exposed filesystem-dependent Claude glob order, which changed cache rowids, the synthetic dirty-row selection and floating aggregate traversal. The pre-fix committed macOS capture was 164,619 bytes at stable_sha256 68a35bfd3605ff49d340d7917cd2755341e62d9292eca7fb110334369fa6b525; the pre-fix Linux matrix capture was 167,944 bytes at stable_sha256 ce5cf47798e378e92da4d8eaa8bca9b0e5c553ed2cd66f2cc85a7e01cd0ba7e4. The reviewed retake is identical at 167,976 bytes and stable_sha256 2140ec6458d64d8c0194f2a31c21bfc0bec5297b42af9f95b6ce8e61bf91154f on native macOS and the pinned Linux Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 images.

envelope._661_s2_retake: #661 S2 moved BOTH envelope values while the corpus fingerprint remained fixed, and the drift is attributed rather than assumed. Stage C added two keys that every envelope carries: `alerts_settings.rate_change_enabled` and `sources.claude.data.budget.settings.rate_change_enabled`, plus the top-level `meter_rate_changes` array, which is empty over this corpus. Nothing in the suite ran `--verify` at that point, so the oracle went stale exactly the way `_583_s3_retake` records it going stale before. The pre-change capture recorded here was 168315 bytes at stable_sha256 bafac0457e24059ecb6197001d07d5b0af94ddfa406169c36f81db4c75b8804b. Stage D3's own change — the additive `forecast.quota` object and the coupled header operands — moved NEITHER value, and that is measured, not assumed: a capture from the tree immediately before D3 and one from the tree immediately after are 168401 bytes at stable_sha256 709ca8cc... on both sides, and a flattened key-by-key comparison of the two envelopes contains no added key, no removed key and no changed value. The reason is that this corpus publishes a null top-level `forecast` and a null `header.dollar_per_pct`, so neither new code path produces output here. The dashboard golden harness is what covers those paths. JSON ESCAPING, recorded because a byte change to a mirrored file that no commit body mentions reads as capture drift to the next person who diffs it: the same edit re-serialized this file's em-dashes as literal characters in place of the escapes they carried before. It did not finish the job at the time: one escape survived, and it survived inside the very sentence that claimed every note string had been converted. Correcting that sentence in the #661 S2 remediation round deleted the surviving escape as a side effect, so the file now carries 12 literal em-dashes and no escapes. Both counts are stated because a bare 'all of them' is what was wrong the first time. That was a HAND edit. `bin/cctally-snapshot-measure` never writes this file — it only reads it at `ORACLE_BASELINE_PATH` to verify against — so no tool chose the encoding. Both forms are valid JSON and parse to the same strings, the load-bearing `bytes`, `stable_sha256` and `corpus.fingerprint` values are untouched by it, and it is left as it stands rather than reverted, since a second re-serialization would be a second unexplained byte change.
envelope._683_corpus_retake: #683 expanded the generated corpus with Claude meta/tool-result messages and Codex subagent threads so the diagnosis-latency acceptance run exercises identity and fan-out discriminators instead of only their empty branches. The corpus fingerprint and generator-owned counts therefore moved. A canonical re-capture measured the same 168401 envelope bytes and the same stable_sha256 709ca8cc2b2ec7e263b7342fcf28992a6b51fce76bdb1d6d4cd385c48c4db7a8, so this is a corpus retake and not a dashboard-envelope contract change.

reproducibility.stable_sha256: The value to assert. sha256 over the envelope with three named field sets removed and NOTHING else — `data_version` at the top level and inside each `sources[*]` entry, the top-level `doctor` object, and the nested `sync_activity.server_epoch`. All three sets are pinned against literals by test so none can grow without a stated reason, and a unit test proves the digest ignores exactly those and still discriminates other content — including each of the six remaining `sync_activity` fields, so a trim that quietly dropped the whole subtree would fail rather than pass.
reproducibility.why_server_epoch_is_excluded: #583 S2. It is a fresh uuid4 minted per SERVER PROCESS, so unlike the other two it moves on every run rather than across a corpus rebuild or between machines — leaving it in would break this oracle continuously instead of moving it once. It is a fixed 16 characters, so `envelope.bytes` stays a meaningful comparison and only the digest excludes it. It is the first NESTED exclusion, which is why it lives in its own set (`_PROCESS_VARIANT_PATHS`) rather than widening either flat tuple.
reproducibility.why_data_version_is_excluded: It is the snapshot signature, and it folds in the wall-clock metadata production ingest stamps. Two captures against one built corpus are byte-identical; after a full rebuild of the same corpus this is the only field that moves. That is also why bin/build-bench-fixtures.py defines its own reproducibility over semantic columns rather than bytes.
reproducibility.why_doctor_is_excluded: It is machine-derived: `counts` summarises 62 host checks and `fingerprint` is a fixed-length sha1 digest over the whole doctor result. Fixed length is why a second machine reproduces the corpus fingerprint and the envelope byte count EXACTLY while disagreeing on a hash over the bytes.
reproducibility.verified_on: MEASURED BY THIS SESSION (#750 S1, 2026-09-04), under TZ=Etc/UTC: a per-leaf envelope diagnostic ran on both LAN runners (two different hosts) against each of two trees, 443e7e842 and 302027f2a. Within each tree the two hosts produced byte-identical envelopes — the same raw sha256, the same stable sha256, the same byte count, the same corpus fingerprint, the same dataset counts, and an equal record for every one of the remaining JSON leaves after the three excluded field sets were removed (6863 leaves at 443e7e842, 6871 at 302027f2a). The envelope therefore tracks the tree and not the host, and there is no machine-dependent field here to exclude. The tested tree at 443e7e842 produced 168401 bytes at stable_sha256 709ca8cc…, which are the values recorded above. A tree digest rather than a commit id identifies what was tested, because a commit hash changes when the file recording it is edited. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 during the #750 S1 review, because the sentence that stood here joined two facts that are not the same fact: it read as if the recorded producer digest identified the tree the four runs executed on. It does not. The four-run diagnostic ran on 443e7e842 and 302027f2a, and NEITHER records a producer digest, because the build-provenance mechanism did not exist on either. The digest recorded in corpus.build_provenance identifies a third tree: this branch's, whose ingest produced the corpus that the numbers above were re-confirmed over during the provenance refresh. RECORDED BY AN EARLIER SESSION AND NOT REPRODUCED HERE: that the same values were also observed under two host timezones (Etc/UTC and Asia/Jerusalem), across a full corpus rebuild, across two consecutive captures against one built corpus, and after #622 on native macOS plus the pinned Linux Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 matrix images. This session neither confirmed nor disproved any of those; they are kept because deleting a claim that was not disproved would replace one unevidenced statement with another. The independence from `doctor` is proven by unit test, so the whole field is a statement about what was measured and what the digest provably ignores, not a claim that any machine anywhere reproduces it.
reproducibility.tz: LOAD-BEARING, and pinned by the tool rather than left to the caller. `display.tz` defaults to `local`, the envelope carries `display.resolved_tz`, and every date-bucketed panel buckets in it. Measured before the pin: the same command under Asia/Jerusalem produced 235,220 bytes against 232,328 under Etc/UTC. bin/cctally-snapshot-measure now sets TZ=Etc/UTC itself.
reproducibility.corpus_root: LOAD-BEARING. Codex identity is derived from the ABSOLUTE canonical provider-root path: `source_root_key` hashes it, and every Codex session key, project key, quota key and history key in the envelope derives from that. A corpus built under a different logical root publishes a different identity universe. `cctally-snapshot-measure` therefore defaults `--corpus-root` to a literal path rather than `tempfile.gettempdir()`. The generator and renderer use the resolved physical root for filesystem access and containment, while an oracle-only scoped alias feeds the literal logical root to identity hashing; this makes macOS `/private/tmp` and Linux `/tmp` spellings of that same requested root byte-identical without changing production identity semantics.
reproducibility.environment: The tool pins the corpus's own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CODEX_HOME and HOME for the measurement and RESTORES them on return, so it can be called as a library. That pinning is part of the capture: the envelope carries HOME/config-dependent keys — `transcriptsEnabled` appears or not depending on the transcript privacy gate — so a capture taken under a different home is a different artefact even with an identical corpus fingerprint. KNOWN NARROWING (#583 S1 review, recorded rather than fixed): the RE-TAKEN capture no longer discriminates `transcriptsEnabled`. The key is present-or-absent depending on the transcript privacy gate, and the corpus home the tool now pins resolves that gate to one state, so a change to it would not move this hash. The environment pinning is still part of the capture contract for every other home-dependent key; this one axis is simply no longer covered, and a gate that needs it must assert it directly rather than rely on this oracle.
reproducibility.reader: `bin/cctally-snapshot-measure --corpus small --verify` is the reader. It re-captures against this file and exits 3 on a mismatch of `stable_sha256`, `envelope.bytes` or `corpus.fingerprint`, reporting all three axes before returning. It compares `stable_sha256` and never the raw one, for the reason recorded above. The pytest estate deliberately does NOT own this check: the corpus root is part of the capture contract, so a pytest tmp directory reproduces a different hash by construction.
